hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try $(1, 0)$ to $(1, 5)$ first, which is $5$ units. Starting from $y = -2$ instead adds the units below the x-axis.
The two points have the same x-coordinate, so one is directly above the other. Only the y-values matter for the distance.
Take the absolute value of the difference of the y-values: $|5 - (-2)|$. Subtracting $-2$ is the same as adding $2$.

explanation: Both points have $x = 1$, so they lie on a vertical line.
The distance on a vertical line is the absolute value of the difference of the y-values: $|5 - (-2)|$.
Subtracting a negative is the same as adding, so this equals $|5 + 2| = 7$.
The distance from $(1, -2)$ to $(1, 5)$ is $7$ units.
